summary.text: Ekman transport is the movement of ocean surface water caused by the wind's friction, part of a theory Vagn Walfrid Ekman first investigated in 1902.
Because of the Coriolis effect, the water moves at an angle to the wind, veering clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and anticlockwise in the Southern.
Where the moved water diverges, deep water is drawn up and upwelling feeds fisheries; where it converges, surface water is pushed down.

facts.label: First noticed by
facts.value: Fridtjof Nansen, watching Arctic ice drift

items.prompt: On an Arctic expedition in the 1890s, an explorer noticed something odd that led to this idea. What was it?

options.label: Ice melted faster in calm water
Ice drifted straight against the wind
Ice drifted at an angle to the wind
Ice stayed still in strong winds

items.explain: Fridtjof Nansen recorded that the ice seemed to move at an angle to the wind direction.

items.prompt: In the Northern Hemisphere, a wind blows due north over the open sea. Which way is the surface water transported?

options.label: Toward the east
Toward the west
Toward the north
Toward the south

items.explain: Transport veers clockwise from the wind in the Northern Hemisphere, at 90°, so a north wind moves water east.

items.prompt: Wind along a coast pulls the surface water away from shore. What fills the space it leaves?

options.label: Warm water pushed down from above
Deep water drawn up from below
Fresh water flowing in from rivers
Nothing; sea level just drops

items.explain: Displaced water must be replaced, so Ekman suction pulls deep water up into the sunlit zone.

items.prompt: Winds over the open subtropical ocean pile surface water up in the middle of a gyre. Why are the waters there poor in nutrients?

options.label: Deep water rises there far too fast
Melting ice dilutes the nutrients
Fish eat every nutrient that arrives
Poor surface water is pumped down

items.explain: The piled-up, nutrient-poor surface water is pumped downward, and this downwelling lowers biological productivity.

items.prompt: Trade winds pull water northward just north of the equator and southward just south of it. What happens at the equator?

options.label: Water piles up and sinks
The ocean surface freezes
Water spreads apart and wells up
The flows cancel and nothing moves

items.explain: The water diverges at the equator, causing Ekman suction and upwelling.

items.prompt: Besides lowering productivity, what does downwelling carry down into the deep ocean?

options.label: Heat and dissolved oxygen
Cold water and nutrients
Sand and river sediment
Sunlight for deep-sea algae

items.explain: Warm, oxygen-rich surface water is pumped down, taking heat and dissolved oxygen with it.
